record.paper_title: Some Open Questions in Analysis for Dirichlet Series
record.original_question: For 0 < p < 1, describe the dual spaces of the Hardy spaces H^p of Dirichlet series.

evidence.quote: Problem 2.8. Describe the dual spaces of Hp.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathscr{P}$ denote the set of Dirichlet polynomials $f(s) = \sum_{n=1}^{N} a_n n^{-s}$. For $0 < p < \infty$, define the Hardy space $\mathcal{H}^p$ of Dirichlet series as the completion of $\mathscr{P}$ with respect to the Besicovitch–type norm
$$\|f\|_{\mathcal{H}^p} = \left( \lim_{T\to\infty} \frac{1}{2T} \int_{-T}^{T} |f(it)|^p \, dt \right)^{1/p},$$
equivalently identified, via the Bohr lift $n = p_1^{\kappa_1} p_2^{\kappa_2}\cdots \mapsto z_1^{\kappa_1} z_2^{\kappa_2}\cdots$ (where $p_j$ is the $j$-th prime), with the Hardy space $H^p(\mathbb{T}^\infty)$ of the infinite-dimensional polytorus equipped with normalized Haar measure.

For $0 < p < 1$, give an explicit description (in terms of Dirichlet series or boundary objects) of the dual space $(\mathcal{H}^p)^*$ of continuous linear functionals on $\mathcal{H}^p$.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of describing the duals of $\mathcal{H}^p$ for $0<p<1$ remains open. Recent work on Hardy spaces of Dirichlet series (e.g. on multipliers, Volterra operators, and linear-space properties) treats partial aspects but does not provide a full description of $(\mathcal{H}^p)^*$ in the range $0<p<1$; even for $1<p<\infty$ the dual is known not to coincide with $\mathcal{H}^q$.

status_evidence.title: Multipliers for Hardy spaces of Dirichlet series
status_evidence.snippet: Studies multipliers and structure of H^p of Dirichlet series; duality questions for 0<p<1 are not resolved.
status_evidence.claim: Recent literature continues to treat structural questions about H^p of Dirichlet series without giving a full description of duals for 0<p<1.

status_evidence.title: Linear space properties of H^p spaces of Dirichlet series
status_evidence.snippet: Examines whether H^p is isomorphic to standard sequence/function spaces; dual identification for p<1 is not provided.
status_evidence.claim: The duals of H^p of Dirichlet series for 0<p<1 are not identified in the available literature.
